andover_climate_lobby.description: Student initiative of the Phillips Academy Sustainability Coalition that takes students to the Massachusetts State House to lobby legislators to co-sponsor climate bills.

belmont_high_school_climate_club.description: Student club at Belmont High School that runs a lunchtime composting program and pushes for less waste across Belmont schools.

northfield_mount_hermon_ecoleaders.description: Student environmental group at Northfield Mount Hermon School that runs climate education events, voter and lobbying activities and upcycling workshops, and hosted a 2024 interschool youth climate summit.

salem_high_school_sustainability_club.description: Student environmental club at Salem High School that lobbies at the State House for air quality, climate education and anti-gas-expansion bills; supported by Salem SAFE.

students_for_environmental_action_at_wes.description: Student club at Weston High School that runs recycling and composting, removes invasive plants, grows lettuce in the school greenhouse and lobbies state legislators on climate bills.

newton_south_high_school_environmental_c.description: Student club at Newton South High School for discussing and learning about climate change and environmental issues.

andover_high_school_environmental_club.description: Student club at Andover High School that runs recycling, composting, garden and e-waste projects and helps other schools start composting.

belmont_hill_sustainability_club.description: Student group at Belmont Hill School (Upper School Sustainability Group) that educates the school community on environmental issues and promotes sustainable change on campus.

lorax_at_milton_academy.description: Student environmental group at Milton Academy, founded in 1987, that raises ecological awareness and promotes responsible practices on campus through discussion and education.

boston_latin_school_youthcan.description: After-school climate club at Boston Latin School that runs a youth climate summit, campaigns for sustainability education in grades 7-12 and coordinates a network of youth climate groups at other Massachusetts schools.

boston_university_environmental_student_.description: Student group at Boston University that holds community service outings, nature trips, guest speakers and documentary screenings to raise awareness of environmental issues.

four_rivers_climate_club.description: Student club at Four Rivers Charter Public School in Greenfield, formed in March 2024, that organizes litter cleanups and climate activism events.

youth_climate_action_now.description: Youth-led group under Climate Action Now that holds monthly workshops, webinars, creative events and advocacy training to get young people involved in climate action.

alternatives_for_community_and_environme.description: Roxbury-based environmental justice organization, founded in 1994, that does community organizing, youth leadership, transit advocacy and legal support for low-income communities and communities of color.

greenroots_eco.description: Youth leadership program of GreenRoots in Chelsea where high school students run environmental justice campaigns on water quality, heat, murals and youth organizing.

tree_boston.description: Dorchester-based nonprofit (formerly Speak for the Trees) that plants and cares for trees and advocates for tree equity in Boston neighborhoods, including a teen urban tree corps.

boston_student_advisory_council.description: Citywide council of Boston Public Schools students that advocates on student issues; climate justice has been a focus, including helping write the district's climate change curriculum.

masscosh_tlaw_climate_change_and_environ.description: Youth program of MassCOSH that trains Boston teens as peer educators and organizers on workplace rights and safety, with a goal of building young labor and environmental justice activists.

clean_water_action.description: Advocacy organization with Boston and Northampton offices that organizes and lobbies in Massachusetts on toxic chemicals, clean energy and climate justice, lead in water, waste reduction and civic engagement.

youth_action_collaborative_alumni_node_a.description: Clean Water Action program that trains high school students from environmental justice communities as advocates on climate justice, PFAS, lead and zero waste; started with a Malden High School cohort, with an alumni chapter planned.

sustainable_sharon_coalition_youth.description: High-school-age interest group within the Sustainable Sharon Coalition, a volunteer-led environmental nonprofit in Sharon.

masspirg.description: State advocacy group of the PIRG network that lobbies on consumer protection, waste reduction, transportation and clean energy, and runs campus chapters.

masspirg_amherst.description: UMass Amherst chapter of the student-run MASSPIRG, active since 1972, with campaigns on campus renewable energy, pollinators, textbook costs and voter registration.

vietaid.description: Community development corporation in Fields Corner, Dorchester, serving the Vietnamese American community with civic engagement, affordable housing, small business help and child care.

mothers_out_front.description: Network of mothers and other caregivers organizing for climate justice; in Massachusetts its main campaign pushes to end new gas pipelines and move neighborhoods to clean heat.

healthlink.description: Grassroots environmental group based in Swampscott focused on reducing pollution and toxins, especially power plant and air pollution, and promoting renewable energy.

jewish_climate_action_network.description: Boston-area Jewish group, founded in 2013, that runs climate education, joins marches and legislative campaigns, and helps synagogues cut energy use and divest from fossil fuels.

massachusetts_interfaith_power_and_light.description: Faith-based nonprofit, founded in 2002, that helps houses of worship cut emissions and organizes people of faith for climate advocacy and climate justice.

the_enviro_show_on_wxoj_lp_103_3_fm.description: Biweekly environmental news and commentary radio show on Valley Free Radio (WXOJ-LP 103.3 FM, Florence), also broadcast in Greenfield and North Adams, covering climate, conservation and local ecology.

xr_youth.description: Youth counterpart of Extinction Rebellion Massachusetts for people 18 and under, using nonviolent direct action to demand government action on the climate emergency.

act_on_mass.description: Massachusetts advocacy group that tracks and backs state legislation (including climate bills such as the Climate Change Superfund bill) and runs campaigns on legislative accountability and transparency.

massachusetts_climate_action_network.description: Network that supports local climate action town by town through local chapters, working with 40+ communities on decarbonization and electrification and advocating on state energy and climate policy.

sustainable_milton.description: Neighbor-driven nonprofit in Milton, founded in 2006, that runs composting, green electricity, waste reduction and cleanup programs and advocates for local climate action.

salem_alliance_for_the_environment.description: Salem environmental advocacy group working on air quality, wind and public power, heat resilience, environmental justice and gas leaks; also supports Salem High School's environmental club.

conservation_law_foundation.description: New England environmental advocacy group, founded in 1966 and headquartered in Boston, that uses law, science and policy on clean energy, clean air and water, oceans and environmental justice.

climate_action_now_western_ma.description: Grassroots volunteer group in Western Massachusetts focused on climate justice organizing and public education; its youth wing is Youth Climate Action Now.

greenroots.description: Chelsea environmental justice organization, about 30 years old, that restores salt marsh, builds parks and waterfront access and works to improve Chelsea Creek water quality, with a youth leadership program.

roxbury_environmental_empowerment_projec.description: Youth-led environmental justice organizing program of ACE that builds leadership among young people of color from Roxbury, Dorchester and Mattapan; led the campaign for Boston's 2015 diesel emissions ordinance.

REEP/Greenroots ECO typed 501c3 because they are programs of 501c3 parents.
